paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers walked along the old town trail with Teacher Kim. The old town was quiet in the morning, and the houses were old and tall. The trail went west, and it went past a small hotel. "Let us enter," said Teacher Kim. "May, today you ask the questions." A woman sat at the front desk, and she smiled at the children.

"What is your job?" asked May. "I work at this desk," said the woman. "I give each guest a key and answer questions." "Do the guests ask you by email?" asked May. "Yes, many guests book a room online," said the woman. "I answer their messages every morning." "Is it a hard job?" asked May. "A little," said the woman. "But I like it, because I meet people from many places." "I speak English with guests every day, and it helps me improve."

"Do you ever have an unfriendly guest?" asked Leo. "Sometimes," said the woman. "But if I smile, the guest usually smiles too." A man came in while she was talking. He had a big bag, and he looked tired. "Good morning," said the woman. "Welcome. Breakfast is ready until ten o'clock." The man smiled and said thank you in English. He took his key and went up the stairs.

Outside, Teacher Kim had a guessing game. "Guess the person," she said. "This person sits at a desk, gives keys, and smiles." "The woman at the hotel," said Mia. "Now guess the place," said Teacher Kim. "People sleep here when they travel, and they eat breakfast here." "A hotel!" said Lily. "Is the hotel in the east or in the west?" asked Teacher Kim. "In the west of the old town," said May.
That evening, May wrote her questions and the answers for Explorers' Blog. "I also want to improve my English," she said. "Perhaps I can work at a hotel one day."
